name: Wedding casual

card.summary: An informal wedding dress code that asks guests to look neat and respectful without full formalwear, so an outfit is easy to get right and still flatters.

quick.overview:
Wedding casual is a dress code printed on invitations to tell guests that formal attire is not expected. Guests are asked to dress respectfully without needing to be fancy.

For looks, it is a styling category: a polished but relaxed outfit, such as a well-fitting shirt and trousers or a simple dress, helps a person look put-together at an event where they will be photographed.
quick.how: Guests choose clean, fitted, wrinkle-free clothes that are a step above everyday wear, and match shoes and grooming to the outfit. The setting, season and time of day inform fabric and colour choices.
quick.risks: The main risk is misreading the code. Hosts differ on what casual means, and invitation wording or the couple's guidance is the usual reference.

lead: Wedding casual is a dress code for wedding guests that sits below formal and semi-formal attire. A general reference on dress codes notes that weddings tend to be formal affairs, with grooms and groomsmen typically in a morning coat, tuxedo or dinner jacket, and describes wedding casual as guests dressing respectfully but not necessarily fancily [1].

It matters for appearance because the clothes, fit and grooming a person chooses determine how they look in photographs and in person. Looksmaxxing discussions of style treat fit, colour and grooming as levers that apply to any dress code, and wedding casual is a setting where they can be applied without formalwear.
No studies were found specifically on wedding casual dress.

angle.text: Wedding casual lets guests look put-together in relaxed clothing. Fit, clean grooming and coordinated shoes are what make an informal outfit look deliberate.

paras: Dress codes grade clothing by formality. Semi-formal is described as having a much less precise definition, usually an evening jacket and tie for men and a dress for women, while casual generally means ordinary clothing for the torso, legs and feet [1]. Wedding casual falls between the two in practice, with the wedding setting prompting a tidier look than everyday casual wear [1].
The term appears as a styling category in discussion of outfits for events. Typical themes are fit, clean grooming and avoiding clothing that reads as too sloppy or too formal for the setting.
